title: Building a lightweight way to track 3D asset production flows for games — with the option to assign work to AI-powered agents
author: Leading-Bison-8916
selftext:
The problem we kept hitting on is that 3D content teams are stuck managing production across 5–6 different tools—Slack, spreadsheets, ShotGrid, Jira, email threads… you name it. That constant jumping between platforms slowed teams down and made creative work feel chaotic.

With Flow, we’re bringing the entire 3D production pipeline into one place. Unlike Jira or ShotGrid, which were never designed for artists, Flow is explicitly built for 3D teams. You can orchestrate your pipeline, track every asset’s stage, and keep your team fully in sync—without losing the creative flow.

Existing features:

* Assigning tasks to team members
* Sharing progress for a 3D asset
* Real-time reviews — with revisions, approvals, and progress tracking all in one view.
* Create saved views and filters to track every asset and keep projects moving with clarity.
* Possibility to outsource specific steps or entire assets to us to remove bottlenecks while staying in control.

What's coming next:

* Build milestones, set deadlines, and design custom workflows tailored to your productions.

Would love feedback from teams feeling similar pain points — what did we miss?

Link: [kaedim3d.com/flow](http://kaedim3d.com/flow)

comments.author: Arepa99
comments.body:
From my experience working in video game companies, managing studio production through several different tools like the ones mentioned makes the process extremely chaotic and inefficient. You end up having to upload screenshots from every angle for a single 3D model, and even then it can’t be fully appreciated unless you take the time to download and import it into a 3D software, which only slows the process down.

Having a platform like Flow, where all these artistic processes can be conveniently found in one place, would greatly facilitate team organization! I’d love to see it implemented in more companies that work on artistic pipelines, as I believe it can contribute a lot to the video game field

comments.author: Conscious_Future5136
comments.body: Do you plan to embed communication methods into the platform, like how Google Doc has a chat or Jira where you can leave comments?

replies.author: Leading-Bison-8916
replies.body:
Good question! Right now, each asset has its own thread where you and your team can leave notes, and track revisions and approvals, so all feedback stays tied to the work itself.

Do you think additional communication methods would be useful? If yes, why?

comments.author: Embarrassed_Court142
comments.body: Sounds cool! How do we design custom workflows? because that might be really helpful for some big studios too.

replies.author: Leading-Bison-8916
replies.body: Thanks! We're working on custom workflows right now. The idea is that you’ll be able to define your own pipeline stages (like Blockout → Sculpt → UV → Texture → Final), set dependencies between them, and decide who owns each stage. You’ll also be able to add custom statuses and milestones, so bigger teams can mirror the exact structure they already use internally—without forcing artists to adapt to a generic PM tool. Curious to hear your thoughts on this!

replies.author: Frisk_Cinnamon_Pie
replies.body:
it means if i work with clients , i could show it to my client?  
i used to work for various 3d models, and usually i upload my models to sketchfab , then give the links in google sheet

replies.author: Leading-Bison-8916
replies.body:
Yes exactly, you can share it directly with your clients.

You just invite them into a teamspace, and they’ll be able to open the asset, view versions, leave feedback, and approve — all in the same place. No need to upload to Sketchfab and paste links anymore; everything (models, comments, approvals) stays tied to the asset itself.
